items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: I wasn't there. That was done at one of the periods when Louie Armstrong was there, before I started into the band.

ctx.x: Oh, you know, I'll take it a little easy. I sort of take things a little easier as it is now. I don't really like to do anything now except make recordings and TV jobs which pay well with short hours. That's what I would like to do for the rest of my life, so far as my working days are concerned. So far as going out and whooping and hollering and stomping my feet and doing that, I hope to never do that again as long as I live because I've proven my point a long time ago.
Okay. When Louie Armstrong came to Sebastian's Cotton Club, had you heard him before on records? That was his first trip to the West Coast, wasn't it?

That was his first trip. Everybody had heard Louie Armstrong that was interested in jazz because the first time I heard Louie Armstrong, actually was with the old, old Fletcher Henderson records, when I was just a little kid.
